definitions.explanation: Something that provokes a physical or mental response.
Something that encourages action or effort.

examples.japanese: コーヒーは{脳|のう}に{刺激|しげき}を{与|あた}える。
examples.english: Coffee provides stimulation to the brain.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{環境|かんきょう}は{良|よ}い{刺激|しげき}になる。
examples.english: A new environment serves as good stimulation.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{成功|せいこう}に{刺激|しげき}されて、{私|わたし}も{挑戦|ちょうせん}することにした。
examples.english: Inspired by his success, I decided to try as well.
examples.notes: 刺激される = to be stimulated/inspired

notes:
{刺激|しげき} refers to anything that provokes a response, whether physical (sensory stimulation) or psychological (motivation, inspiration).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {刺激|しげき}を{与|あた}える (to give/provide stimulation)
- {刺激|しげき}を{受|う}ける (to receive stimulation)
- {刺激|しげき}になる (to serve as stimulation)
- {刺激|しげき}される (to be stimulated/inspired)

COLLOCATIONS:
- {強|つよ}い{刺激|しげき} (strong stimulation)
- {良|よ}い{刺激|しげき} (good stimulation)
- {経済|けいざい}{刺激|しげき}{策|さく} (economic stimulus measures)

USAGE NOTE:
As a suru-verb, {刺激|しげき}する means "to stimulate" (transitive). The passive form {刺激|しげき}される often means "to be inspired" when referring to motivation.
